name: Misty Forest — Wanderings in the Mist
description: Eerie, low-stakes travel encounters for the trek through the Misty Forest, on the way to the Hidden Temple — mood and roleplay, never a real threat (monsters instinctively shun this wood). NONE of these reveal the truth of the forest. Three entries — the sourceless song (03), the carved heart naming CORIN (07), and the shared dream if they camp (12) — carry very nascent, deniable hints of the Dreamer, her lost love, and the grief bleeding out of her; let them pass as fey strangeness, an old carving, and an uncanny dream. Four entries (02, 04, 06, 08) hand the party a small keepsake to keep. Rollable on any leg of the journey through the wood.

results.description:
The Watching Doe — a pale, dapple-grey doe stands square in the path and does not startle, does not flee — she simply watches, the long, patient way a person watches, not an animal. Hold her gaze and there is something almost like recognition in it. The moment anyone steps toward her she is not there — no bound, no crash of brush, just gone, and the mist where she stood.
GM — set the tone with this one: nothing in this wood behaves quite the way an animal should. No check reveals anything; she is simply wrong, and gone.

The Out-of-Season Hollow — the path dips into a warm hollow full of spring flowers in full, dewy bloom, though the trees standing over them are bare and the air everywhere else is cold. It smells of a May morning that should not exist here. Nothing harms anyone who lingers; it is just gently, insistently wrong.
GM — a party member may pick a blossom that never wilts. Gives the party: Everbloom Petal. @UUID[Item.L0KVk7cq1YT2u06k]{Everbloom Petal}

The Song With No Singer — somewhere just ahead a woman is humming, low and slow and unbearably sad, an old tune half-remembered. Follow it and it is always around the next trunk — never closer, never farther — and it fades the instant they stop trying to find her. No one is ever there.
GM — nascent clue: the Dreamer's grief, leaking into the wood as a song (the same melody as the ballad "The Green and the Grey" from the Trade Way table, if a player makes the leap). Let it stay a sad, sourceless tune; reveal nothing.

The Fairy Ring — a flawless ring of pale mushrooms in a clearing, the grass inside greener than anywhere around it. Stepping inside does nothing magical at all — but everyone who does feels, for a single heartbeat, the certainty that they have stood here before and were happy. They have not.
GM — harmless; the old fairy-ring dread is a bluff here. A player who picks a cap keeps it. Gives the party: Fey Ring Cap. @UUID[Item.Q8ZpqxiZU7FdVllM]{Fey Ring Cap}

The Mirror Pond — a small pool so perfectly still it holds the sky like glass. But the sky it holds is a clear, warm blue afternoon — while overhead it is grey, and misted, and drawing on toward evening. Drop a stone and the ripples clear to show the wrong sky again.
GM — pure mood. If someone insists on reading meaning into it, they see nothing but the borrowed afternoon.

The Toy in the Roots — wedged into the roots of an old tree, a child's carved wooden fox, weathered soft but somehow un-rotted, as if set down a moment ago. There is no village for a day in any direction. No sign of who left it, or when, or why it is still faintly warm.
GM — a quiet ache of loss with no answer attached. A player may pocket it. Gives the party: Carved Wooden Fox. @UUID[Item.huzmudEOBsJ7gt6L]{Carved Wooden Fox}

The Carved Heart — an old beech grown broad and grey, and cut into its bark long ago: a heart, and two names. One reads CORIN. The other has been worn — or wept — away to nothing. The cut is decades old, yet clear sap still beads along it, slow, like a wound that never learned to close.
GM — nascent clue: the Dreamer and her lost mortal love. Play it as any old lovers' carving; do not tie it to anything yet. If they ask around later, no one local has ever heard the name.

The Lost Traveller — a man in old-fashioned dress walks the other way, unhurried and courteous. He greets the party warmly and asks — with gentle, genuine confusion — what year it is, and whether the war is over. Which war? He cannot quite say. He thanks them all the same, presses a coin into someone's hand for the kindness, tips his hat, and walks on into the mist.
GM — the wood does not keep time. He is decades — centuries? — adrift, and does not know it. Gives the party: Worn Half-Penny. @UUID[Item.4TIJfxrcBRkgldi4]{Worn Half-Penny}

The Offering-Willow — a great willow whose trailing branches are hung with hundreds of little tokens: ribbons, buttons, carved beads, locks of hair, a tin ring — offerings tied here by countless hands over what must be centuries. Taking one feels unspeakably wrong. Leaving one feels right.
GM — an RP beat, not a trap. If a player ties on a small offering of their own, nothing "happens" — but for the next hour the wood feels a shade gentler and the mist a little thinner. Let them feel noticed.

The Swallowed Cart — a merchant's cart, abandoned so long that saplings have grown up through its bed and moss has furred every plank; the forest is quietly eating it. Nothing of worth remains — but a tin cup still sits upright on the driver's seat, as though set down a moment ago and simply never picked back up.
GM — mood. How long has it stood here? The cup says no time at all; the saplings say a lifetime. Both are true.

The Fox That Leads — a small red fox trots along the path ahead, stops, looks back over its shoulder, and plainly waits to be followed. It leads them a while — truer and easier toward the shrine than the mist should allow — then slips sideways into the ferns and is gone.
GM — a small kindness from the wood. Use it to nudge a lost or dithering party back toward the Hidden Temple; nothing sinister, this once.

The Shared Dream (only if the party rests or camps in the wood) — everyone who sleeps here wakes from the same dream: a green and sunlit place, a golden-haired woman with her back turned, and a grief so vast there are no words inside it. No one remembers more than that. They wake unrested, and oddly reluctant to speak of it aloud.
GM — nascent clue, and the strongest of them: the Dreamer, and the shared dreams that spread from her. Still deniable — a shared dream is uncanny, not proof. Do not name her; let the wrongness sit.
